theHeartTagline: The living core of Elarion - if it falls, the village falls.
_guardianLegacyNote: Retired title  -  the player is now 'the Keeper' (STORYLINE.md §4). Preserved so any v1 data reference does not hard-error.
_bossSyndrathNote: Apex village wave-boss (the Black Dragon). NOT from narrative-bible.md / story.ts  -  agent-authored content the owner pulled in and ratified 2026-05-19 (see docs/port-notes/dragon-boss.md §1). Keyed here as a proper noun so the HUD / boss bar never hardcodes it; the displayed name can be re-pointed without touching code.
heartWingDescription: Elarion's airborne aspect; Elarion sometimes walks the sky and the Folk call it the Heart-Wing.
tunnelOrigin: made by the Heart's own roots
_tunnelNameNote: WO-1044 R1/R2, owner ruling 2026-08-17 ('yes to all defaults on 1044'). RETIRED: 'The Hollow Roads'. That name read as THE HOLLOWED'S roads, which promises enemies inside a graph that deliberately authors zero encounters (nine rooms, no traps, no keys, no chests) -- so the player walked an empty crossroads and concluded content was missing. 'The Rootways' explains the quiet as lore: the Heart's song runs down there, so the rot does not; and it explains why the tunnel reaches exactly the four marches, because roots reach where the wards are. THE ID IS DELIBERATELY NOT RENAMED: the scene/graph id stays 'dg_hollow_roads' (BiomeRoads.TunnelSceneId), a contract shared by BiomeRoads.ArmRoomIdFor, dg_hollow_roads.json (dual copy), HollowRoadsDropInjector and BiomeRoadsRegression. Ids are live contracts; display names are not. Pinned by BiomeRoadsRegression Case 7, which fails both if this key drifts from BiomeRoads.TunnelDisplayName and if the retired name returns.
_regionNamesNote: WO-1044 R3, owner ruling 2026-08-17. Code said 'Stoneback'/'Ashwood' while narrative canon said 'Stoneback Ridge'/'Corrupted Ashwood'; the two disagreed. RULED: the SHORT forms are the UI names (they fit the travel prompt, 'Travel to Ashwood (deadly)'), and the LONG forms are PROSE ONLY -- narrative docs, region intro voice lines, quest text. The RUNTIME authority is ZoneManager.Regions, never this file: these keys are the canon RECORD so the ruling has a home outside a markdown doc, and BiomeRoadsRegression Case 3 fails if the short forms here ever drift from that table.
bibleTitleTagline: Tend the Heart. Hold the dark.
_taglineLegacyNote: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-24 (owner directive, Pets→Echoes rebrand)  -  the single canonical title tagline is now 'Echoes of a Forgotten Civilization' (the Echoes are the awakened essences of the people the Heart of Elarion once guarded); tagline AND titleTagline both carry it so whichever the UI reads is correct. The prior tagline 'Hold the line' (WO-570) plus the earlier 'Hold the Chord. Defend the Spire.', 'Hold the chord. Hold the dark.', and bibleTitleTagline 'Tend the Heart. Hold the dark.' plus the Spire/Chord/Lantern/Stone-Choir motifs are RETIRED; bibleTitleTagline is kept here as a historical reference only.

_buildingWordsNote: STOP: THESE KEYS ARE catalog ids AND structures-catalog.json IS THE SINGLE NAMING AUTHORITY (WO-1161, straightened 2026-08-23; this block corrected the same day). They are a convenience mirror for surfaces that resolve a building word by id (VillageStrings.Canon) and they must AGREE with that file's displayName, never lead it. WARNING: UNTIL 2026-08-23 THIS BLOCK CARRIED THE RETIRED WO-840 INVERSION - 'workshop' read 'Forge' and 'forge' read 'Armorer' - so a surface reading canon-strings rendered a DIFFERENT word than one reading the catalog for the SAME id, which is exactly how 'Iron - NEEDS: Forge' was printed to a player whose ledger already held 'forge'. Names are derived from what a building DOES (vendors.json): 'forge' sells WEAPONS -> 'Forge'; 'armorer' sells ARMOUR -> 'Armorer'; 'workshop' is not a vendor -> 'Crafting Station'. If a name must move, move it in structures-catalog.json FIRST and mirror it here in the same edit. IDS ARE FROZEN SAVE KEYS - only the words move. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu).
_upgradeQueueNote: WO-1045. The building upgrade button's QUEUE-FULL face. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). These are the only NEW words that WO authored: the refusal SENTENCES it shows come live from BuildTimerService.LineFullMessage / TryBuySlot and are deliberately NOT duplicated here  -  two copies of a refusal is the drift bug the WO closes. upgradeQueueFullDetail's {0}/{1} are DEPTH (items lined up, queueDepthPerLine=5); upgradeQueueCrews' {0}/{1} are CONCURRENCY (jobs running at once, freeBuildSlots=2). Never swap those: exhausted concurrency QUEUES, only exhausted depth REFUSES, and the remedies differ.
_upgradeShortfallNote: WO-1037. The building upgrade button's MISSING-RESOURCES face - the shortfall band (dead state + harvest path on the wider half, ONE impulse-pack offer on the narrower one). ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). upgradeShortDetail {0}=units still needed, {1}=resource word; upgradeShortHarvest {0}=resource word, lowercased by the View - it is FIRST and on the WIDER half on purpose (WO-1037 section 1: the harvest path stays first-class, the pack is the alternative, never the recommended route). upgradeShortPackOffer {0}=pack name, {1}=amount granted, {2}=resource word, {3}=USD reference price; its embedded newline splits the pack's NAME from its NUMBERS so neither has to be truncated on the narrow plate. upgradeShortPackSoon is the INERT plate's own label: the offer cannot purchase (FeatureFlags.RealmStorePurchase is off AND this surface has no purchase route at all - WO-1037 section 2 / WO-931), and its only action is to dismiss for that upgrade this session. Do NOT reword it into a Buy call-to-action while the plate is inert - a CTA over a rail that cannot transact is precisely the WO-931 defect this ticket was written to avoid repeating.

_dailyChestCopyNote: WO-1051 DAILY CHEST copy (the once-per-UTC-day retention panel, DailyChestController). ASCII only - TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu. These chest* keys are the DAILY CHEST panel and are unrelated to the WO-1132 loot-chest pair above (chestOpenPrompt / chestCombatRefusal), which is world-interaction copy. The ad CTA has THREE worded states - chestClaimDouble (ready) / chestAdNotReady / chestAdOpening - because the owner is red/green colourblind and the button used to carry its state in a face colour that never even changed; the WORD is the carrier and the face colour is only a redundant second channel. The acknowledgement raised as the daily-chest panel closes, for BOTH claim paths (free 500 and rewarded_double 1,000) - DailyChestController.AcknowledgeClaim via ElarionUiKit.ShowToast. Before this key the grant landed in total silence, so a successful double reward and a CANCELLED ad looked identical from the player's seat. {0} is the amount, already thousands-formatted by the caller (invariant culture, so it reads 1,000 exactly as chestBody promises). The word 'Gold' is spelled out beside it: the sentence must name the amount AND the currency in WORDS, ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu), and the toast tone is decoration only - the owner is red/green colourblind, so no meaning may ride on the card colour.

_nightMarketNote: WO-1050 THE NIGHT MARKET (2026-08-21) - the store presentation copy. ASCII only. THE RULE THESE SENTENCES ARE WRITTEN TO: the shelf may only advertise what the grant seam actually pays, and no sentence may imply the GAME holds SKR. SKR is Solana Mobile's own governance token - the owner did not mint it, does not own it and is not releasing a token; there is NO in-game SKR ledger, earn loop or spend loop and there must never be one. storeBalance* are a READ-ONLY MIRROR of the players OWN wallet, read through SolanaWalletProvider.GetBalance, never written, never granted, never deducted in-game - which is why the copy says your wallet and never your SKR. The four storeBalance states are deliberately DISTINCT sentences: no wallet connected is NOT the same fact as a zero balance, and neither is an unreadable one. A confident 0 SKR would launder three different facts (genuinely none / SKR mint unprovisioned in this build / the RPC failed) into one number, which is the same defect class that hid keepers-satchel. storeBalanceFiat is APPROXIMATE by construction - it is derived from a live Jupiter quote that moves between render and purchase - so it keeps its tilde and is DROPPED entirely rather than shown stale or invented. storeTrustTreasury names the on-chain Rewards Distributor account and says nothing about what it holds. WO-1334 (2026-09-03) OWNER RULING (SUPERSEDED FORM, then RE-RULED the same day): the header wallet chip is ONE LINE and reads storeBalanceValue only. The earlier form SKR: <balance> is RETIRED - she reconsidered out loud: 'Maybe we could put the word balance and then put their SKR total ... I see every other site in the world does it ... in the top left put their balance of what they have just in SKR so they know what they can afford immediately.' So the sentence is now Balance: {0} SKR - the WORD Balance leads, because that is the storefront convention she is naming and the word is what makes the number legible as spendable. The chip also MOVED to the TOP LEFT of the panel and gained a dark ground behind it: her words were 'it shouldnt be on the top right hand side and white where its over top of everything else, because thats just ugly, it doesnt make sense and you cant read it.' White text over busy panel art is a stated READABILITY DEFECT, not a taste note, so the chip is drawn on the same black plate idiom the rest of this screen already uses. The truncated base58 address is REMOVED from storeBalanceBoundAddress entirely (her words: they dont need address), so that key no longer takes a {0}. The word Connected is deliberately absent from the connected state because a balance that renders at all already proves the wallet is connected; the DISCONNECTED states are where the words must be explicit, which is why every other storeBalance* sentence names its state in words and never by colour (the owner is red/green colourblind). The old network-frame.png plate that baked Mainnet, a green dot and a Ready pill into the texture is GONE - it printed Mainnet over a Devnet session, which is a confident lie on the surface that takes real money; the network is now read live from WalletService.NetworkLabel and appended to the chip ONLY when it is not mainnet, so a WORD means the tokens are free and silence means real money. storeBalanceFiat is kept but is currently UNRENDERED - its only reader was the chip's ~$ tail.
_storeWordmarkNote: WO-1398 (2026-09-05). storeWordmark is the store's ONE player-facing name. Every face that opens the store renders THIS row and nothing else: the HUD card (HudKitController.BuildNightMarketCard), the Realm deck card (PlayerDeckWorkspace), the Play skin title (GooglePlayStorefront) and the store panel title (PackStore). Two readers, one key: HudStrings.KeyStoreWordmark (Core) and StoreStrings.KeyWordmark (Wallet) both name storeWordmark. Before this note the HUD card said Night Market, the gear dock row said Night Market but opened the Realm deck, and the deck card said Realm Store - four names for one door, typed at four call sites. Change the store's name HERE and every face follows; typing it anywhere else fails StoreNameSingleSourceRegression. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). The HUD card label plate is measured against this exact string by HudLabelFitRegression [night-market-standout] at the 20 px hard floor - a longer name must still fit on one line.

_storeBuyGateNote: WO-1121 store BUY GATE, owner rulings 2026-08-21. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). Every one of these is a REFUSAL the player can act on - none of them is a dead button and none of them says 'the flag is off'. storeBuyClosed: purchases are not open at all in this build. storeBuyRailNotReady: the flag is on but the payment rail has no resolvable mint, so a tap could not settle - said BEFORE any charge. storeBuyWalletRequired: the price-gated refusal - packs above $4.99 need a connected wallet because a guest save key is device-derived and a lost $49.99 entitlement is a chargeback; {0} is the threshold, formatted from PurchaseGate.WalletRequiredAboveUsd so the sentence can never drift from the constant, and it must keep saying what the player CAN still buy. storeBuyWalletRequiredCta / storeBuyComingSoon are the card's right-rail button faces. _storePiSkinNote: WO-1323 THE PI SKIN'S STORE COPY (2026-09-02). ASCII only. WHY THESE EXIST: the owner opened the Night Market signed in as Pi, in real Pi Browser, and every price on the shelf read in SKR - a token this game has never held, never minted and does not own, quoted at a player who cannot spend it. SKR is Solana Mobile's governance token; showing it to a Pi player is the same error the storeBalance note above forbids, pointed at the wrong audience. THE RULE THESE SENTENCES ARE WRITTEN TO: under the Pi skin the CLIENT NEVER COMPUTES A PI PRICE. Every Pi figure on the shelf came back from /api/pi/quote, which prices from the CoinGecko low_24h floor server-side and fails closed; there is no USD-to-Pi converter on this side and there must never be one, because a client that can price is a second pricing authority and WO-1318's whole security model is that the server is the only one. So each sentence below is what the store says INSTEAD of a number: storePiPriceAtCheckout when the price is knowable but has not been quoted yet, storePiNotOnSale when this pack is not on the Pi rail at all, storePiRailUnavailable when Pi itself is not reachable, and storePiShelfEmpty when NOTHING on the shelf is Pi-purchasable - which is an honest state and is deliberately shown as one rather than papered over by falling back to the SKR figures. storePiHeaderNotice replaces the wallet/balance chip, which mirrors a Solana wallet the Pi player does not have. storePiWalletGate is the guest-ceiling refusal reworded for Pi: {0} is PurchaseGate.WalletRequiredAboveUsd, formatted from the constant so it cannot drift, and it must keep saying what the player CAN still buy.

_hudChipCopyNote: WO-1144 HUD chip/face copy, shortened AT SOURCE after the 2026-08-22 headed-fleet capture (break_24_error.png) showed 'Tap to collec' cut mid-word on the Collectors chip and 'Manag...' ellipsised on the Manage bar face. NEITHER was a font bug: the Collectors chip is 220 ref px wide (== EchoUnlockFeedback.EchoChipWidthPx, a fixed rail width three chips share) so its label rect is ~202 ref px, and the action line 'Tap to collect' measures ~214 ref px at the 30 px FontFloor - it could not fit at ANY legible size. The Manage bar face is one sixth of a 46%-wide ActionBar zone, ~144 ref px of label rect, so the WO-1027 session-shape sentence 'Manage - 2 of 3 idle' was about 4x too long for the box it renders in. The fix is SHORTER WORDS HERE, never a smaller font (FontFloor/MinTouchPx are floors, not budget) and never a wider chip (the three rail chips share one right edge). ASCII only - TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu. Pinned by HudLabelFitRegression, which MEASURES each of these strings against its real box using the real font's glyph advances, at both landscape capture aspects.

_raidOutcomeCopyNote: WO-1378, from docs/CREATIVE_CANON_ELARION_2026-09-04.md sections 8.1-8.3. THREE OUTCOMES, THREE DISTINCT SCREENS, AND THEY MUST NOT BE MERGED: a WON raid, a LOST raid, and a MANUAL RETREAT are different things that happened to the player and the canon gives each its own title. The failure copy is what makes the map's deliberately generous 15-20 percent failure payout DIEGETIC - you do not lose the memory, you fail to reclaim it - so a shared 'Defeat' screen would throw away the reason the number exists. ASCII only (TMP renders non-ASCII as tofu). No meaning is carried by colour: the owner is red/green colourblind, so every outcome is a SENTENCE. THESE KEYS ARE THE CANON RECORD AND ARE NOT WIRED YET - the raid result surfaces do not read them as of this edit; naming the keys here is what lets the next lane point at them instead of hardcoding a fourth copy of the sentence (the duplicated-state failure CLAUDE.md sections 2/5/16 are all about). Follow-up: name them as consts on DeNelle.Core.UI.RaidStrings, which is where every other raid string key lives.

_realmVigilNote: WO-1378, creative canon section 5 - the collision between two ladders both called 'threat' is resolved by NAME, not by number. THREAT stays with the endless Iron Bastion ladder (Threat I / II / III, +8 percent enemy strength and +5 percent loot per level) and is deliberately NOT keyed here. The WEEKLY 1-10 climb is the REALM VIGIL: Vigil I through Vigil X, reset weekly, and a reset is the beginning of a NEW Vigil rather than the loss of an old one. It passes the only test a weekly ladder has to pass - 'What Vigil did you reach this week?'. Not wired: no surface reads these keys yet.
_hireReinforcementsNote: WO-1378, creative canon section 6.
